g.text: so the batch dimension is the basin dimension. A single LSTM, with weights shared across basins, reads the same 270-day window of 6 daily
forcings and 30 static catchment attributes for each basin and returns its last hidden state; stacked, these give h. Rows are basins
throughout: blue rows are the 455 gauged basins of the fold, which form the fixed donor pool, and amber rows the 76 held-out ungauged
basins. At inference every basin is a query, so queries supply Q while donors supply K and V. The self-diagonal of the logits is set to
minus infinity in training and in evaluation, so a gauged query cannot read its own row; an ungauged query is not in the pool and
therefore keeps all 455 donors. Here tau is a learned softmax temperature. The attended context c re-enters through a LayerNorm residual.
Dropout at p = 0.4 is applied twice, marked on the diagram: once to ctx on the way into the head, and again between the head's two
layers. The head is a two-layer MLP, 256 to 256 to 1, with ReLU, and emits flow in mm day-1. The three variants differ only inside the
shaded block: vanilla removes it and predicts from h_q alone; spatial keeps it with V = h_d; donor adds the teal term q_d, an encoding of
each donor's own recent discharge. Its flow over days t-6..t enters as a standardised log-flow anomaly, which is dimensionless and so
transfers between basins of very different size, alongside one 1/0 flag per day recording whether that gauge reported -- 14 values per
donor, passed through a small MLP to 256 dimensions and added to h_d. A donor with no observation anywhere in the window is dropped from
the softmax altogether; that masking is applied identically in spatial, so the donor pool is the same in both. During training only the
455 gauged basins are encoded and queried, each masked out of its own row, and the 76 ungauged basins are absent altogether. At no stage
does a query basin's own discharge, or any statistic of it, enter the forward pass.
